title: Company-wide policies and processes (access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, templates)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended for all employees, people managers, and owners of systems and services. Where a section references a team, that team owns the operational practice and is responsible for keeping the section current.

Primary owners and contacts
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team) — Ava Chen (policy owner)
- Security contact (access & data): Harper Singh (eng-security@redwood.example.com)
- Procurement lead: Liam Patel (finance@redwood.example.com)
- Vendor & contracts: Sofia Martinez (legal@redwood.example.com)
- Travel & expenses: Eva Park (people-ops@redwood.example.com)

1) Access & permissions (RBAC and least privilege)
Intro: Access to Redwood systems follows a role-based, least-privilege model with department-aligned role templates and timebound elevations where necessary. All access requests must be auditable and approved by a designated owner.

Key rules:
- Principle of least privilege: default to read-only access; request elevated privileges only when required and justified.
- Role templates: use team-provided role templates in IAM (examples: eng-runtime-ops, eng-data-science, finance-analyst).
- Approvals: every access request requires approval from the resource owner and the requestor's manager for non-admin roles. Admin-level requests require a secondary approver from Security.
- Timebound access: temporary (just-in-time) access maximum duration is 7 days by default; extensions require reapproval.
- Onboarding/offboarding: HR notifies Identity & Access team via HR -> IT integration; access must be provisioned within 24 business hours of onboarding and revoked within 8 hours of termination.

Process (request -> grant):
1. Submit request via Access Request Form (Confluence link & SSO portal).
2. Resource owner reviews justification and assigns role template.
3. Manager approves.
4. IAM system provisions access, records request ID, and notifies requestor.
5. Access is audited monthly; anomalies are flagged to Security.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Provisioning SLA: 24 business hours for standard requests; 4 hours for priority business-critical requests.
- Audit cadence: monthly automated audit reports, quarterly manual review for high-risk privileges.

2) Change management
Scope: Applies to infrastructure, production services, deployment pipelines, and high-impact configuration changes. Low-risk routine changes (e.g., small config tweaks on dev) should follow lightweight approval but still be logged.

Change categories:
- Standard/low-risk: pre-approved, repeatable changes (low-risk config updates).
- Normal: requires CAB review (scheduled window) before deployment.
- Emergency: applied outside change window; requires post-implementation review and retro approval from CAB.

Procedure (normal change):
1. Create Change Request (CR) in Change Log (Jira/Change board) with: owner, impact, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window.
2. Peer review by service owner.
3. CAB review: scheduled weekly; includes representatives from Eng-SRE, Eng-Platform, Security, and Product.
4. Approved changes are scheduled during change windows (standard windows: Tue/Wed 02:00–05:00 UTC).
5. Execute, monitor, and validate.
6. Close CR with post-change notes and retrospective if anomalies occurred.

Emergency change process (summary):
- Emergency CR created with emergency flag.
- Emergency approver (SRE oncall + Security lead) signs off verbally; change executed.
- Postmortem and CAB sign-off within 3 business days.

Rollback and testing requirements:
- Every normal/standard change must include a tested rollback plan.
- Staging or canary deployment required for any change that can affect user-facing latency or correctness.

3) Data management (classification, retention, encryption, backups)
Data classification levels:
- Public: data intended for external distribution.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal data (default).
- Confidential: business-sensitive (financial plans, contracts).
- Restricted: customer or regulated data with strict controls (PII, health data).

Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: all Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access control: Restricted data requires documented business justification and Security approval before access.
- Logging & monitoring: access to Restricted datasets must be logged with at least 90-day retention of access logs; alerts for anomalous access patterns.

Retention & backups:
- Default retention: Internal — 1 year; Confidential — 7 years (where legally required); Restricted — as per contractual/regulatory requirement.
- Backups: daily incremental, weekly full backups for production datasets. Offsite encrypted backups stored in multiple regions for disaster recovery.

Data residency and export control:
- Data that is subject to residency constraints must be stored only in allowed regions per contract (see vendor contracts for customer-specific rules).
- Export of Restricted data outside approved regions requires Legal & Security sign-off.

Data deletion and disposition:
- Follow documented deletion workflows with proof-of-deletion. Managers must certify required deletions for regulatory obligations.

4) Procurement & expenses
Overview: All purchases must follow procurement thresholds and approval flows to ensure budget compliance and vendor vetting.

Approval matrix (examples):
- <= $2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,001–$25,000: Director approval + Finance notification.
- $25,001–$250,000: VP approval + Procurement/Legal review.
- > $250,000: Executive approval + Legal & Procurement.

Procurement workflow:
1. Create purchase requisition in Procurement system with business justification, budget code, and owner.
2. Finance validates budget availability.
3. Legal runs vendor checklist for contracts and risk.
4. Procurement issues PO and tracks delivery.
5. Invoice routed to Finance for payment; receipts attached in expense system.

Company card and expenses:
- Company card holders must follow the expense policy; receipts required for all transactions.
- Per diem and reimbursement limits (see Travel section).

5) Vendor management and onboarding
Vendor risk assessment:
- All vendors must complete a vendor intake form and a security questionnaire appropriate to risk level. Risk levels: Low, Medium, High.
- High-risk vendors (access to customer data, production systems) require SOC2/reporting, security attestation, and an executed Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
1. Business case and owner assigned.
2. Legal review of contract and DPA.
3. Security questionnaire and technical assessment.
4. Procurement creates PO and payment terms.
5. Operational onboarding (access, onboarding docs, escalation contacts).

SLA & performance monitoring:
- Vendor SLAs must include uptime, maintenance windows, response time, and escalation contacts.
- Quarterly vendor reviews for vendors with Active > $50k annual spend or High-risk status.

Offboarding and termination:
- Revoke access, remove credentials, collect assets, and certify data return/deletion according to contract.
- Legal and Procurement coordinate termination steps and evidence of compliance.

6) Travel and expenses
Booking and approvals:
- All business travel must be pre-approved by a manager and submitted via the Travel Request form.
- Preferred suppliers and travel agency must be used for bookings to ensure negotiated rates.

Per diem and reimbursement limits (examples):
- Domestic (US): meals up to $75/day; incidentals up to $25/day.
- International: meals up to $120/day; incidentals up to $40/day.
- Air travel: economy for flights < 6 hours; premium economy for > 6 hours unless exec-approved.
- Hotel: business or standard corporate rate; upgrades require manager approval.

Expense submission and timelines:
- Submit expense report within 14 days of trip completion with itemized receipts.
- Expenses submitted > 60 days may require additional approval and justification.

Safety & emergency policy:
- Employees traveling for work must register trip with People Ops. In case of emergency, contact People Ops and local emergency services.

7) Internal templates and examples (quick links)
This section collects commonly used templates to standardize requests and reduce approval friction. Attach/use the templates in the Confluence Templates library.
- Access Request Form (template) — fields: system, role template, justification, expiration date, resource owner, manager approval.
- Change Request template — fields: change owner, impact, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, CAB notes.
- Vendor Intake form — fields: business owner, vendor legal name, primary contact, risk level, required contracts.
- Travel Request template — fields: traveler, purpose, itinerary, budget code, manager approval.
- Expense report template — itemized, with receipts upload link.

Appendices
- Glossary: RBAC = Role-Based Access Control; CAB = Change Advisory Board; DPA = Data Processing Agreement; KMS = Key Management Service.
- Escalation contacts: Security oncall: security-oncall@redwood.example.com; Finance procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com; Travel & People Ops: people-ops@redwood.example.com.
